answer: Muon flux attestation anchors each agent to a unique underground detector. A newcomer samples 48 hours of coincidence timestamps, hashes them into a Merkle root, and submits a zk-SNARK proving tundra-depth geometry matches a registered coordinate. Peers verify against a comet-epoch randomness beacon, preventing precomputation. The registry will harbor one identity per detector cell. Cloning 10,000 identities requires distinct arrays costing $2.1M in scintillator hardware plus 480,000 detector-hours, making swarm attacks ruinous, like expecting uniform geology across separate boreholes.
